meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'гласить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to invite, to call in', paired with 'приглашать'.

examples.trans: Call your witness.
He invited me over.
Very well. Call your witness.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to punish', paired with 'наказывать'.

examples.trans: History will punish them.
Mum will punish him.
To punish the blind?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pay, to pay off', paired with 'оплачивать'.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt!

examples.text: Он уже оплатил счёт в ресторане.
examples.trans: He has already paid the bill at the restaurant.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины! Клянусь, весь долг!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt! I swear, the whole debt!

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common feminine noun meaning 'dry cleaner’s' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Зайди в химчистку и возьми мой костюм.
examples.trans: Go to the dry cleaners and take my suit.
I can pay for your dry cleaning.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.trans: A big city.
The sum is very large.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'experience, experiment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You will need my rich experience.
This life experience is very valuable.

examples.text: А вот тут вам понадобится мой опыт.
examples.trans: And right here you will need my experience.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
That's mine.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'помнить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remember, to memorise', paired with 'запоминать'.

examples.trans: Remember this word.
I didn't remember his name.

examples.text: Вот так на митингах говори, запомни.
examples.trans: That's how you talk at rallies, remember that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'both', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You both leave here right now.
Get over here right now, quickly, both of you!

examples.text: Вы сейчас отсюда оба уходите. И больше сюда не возвращаетесь. Ясно?
examples.trans: You both leave here right now. And you never come back here again. Clear?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'soul, heart' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Why are you hovering over me?
A kind soul.

examples.text: У меня на душе сильная тревога.
examples.trans: I have a strong anxiety in my soul.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('decent, respectable').

examples.trans: He put on a decent clean suit.

examples.text: В приличном костюме меня никто не узнает.
examples.trans: In a decent suit nobody will recognize me.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'place; seat' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is my seat.
It's a nice place here.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'egg' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Берём свежие яйца и разогреваем сковороду.
examples.trans: We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'the heck, away (colloq.)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нафига ты что бы тарелку сразу брал?
examples.trans: Why on earth did you grab all those plates at once?

examples.text: Не так, чтобы знать, нафиг случай.
examples.trans: Not that I need it right now, just in case.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.
Look who's talking.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'plate, platter, dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.
Put clean plates on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
I understood at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.trans: I'm not taking the knife.
Chef, I didn't take it.
We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of; from behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'over there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's our house, over there.
There he is!
There's chicken, over there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: So much gum!
How much is it?
So much gum! Cool!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish; course' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to redo, to remake', paired with 'переделывать'.

examples.trans: All of this needs to be redone.

examples.text: Я рада. Только всё это нужно переделать.
examples.trans: I'm glad. Only all of this needs to be redone.
Only all of this needs to be redone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.trans: I didn't hear anything.
Can you hear me?

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: That's what you said.
I speak Russian.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('guilty, at fault, to blame').

examples.trans: I know it's my fault.

examples.text: Она ни в чём не виновата.
examples.trans: She is not to blame for anything.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не гони меня. Я знаю, что я виноват.
examples.trans: Please, don't chase me away. I know it's my fault.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Of course I'll help.
Yes, of course.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?
